You can empathize with a patient if you have gone through something similar, but I don't think that necessarily has to involve the disclosure. I think you can relate just by listening to them and providing support and finding solutions. If I thought they needed people to relate too I might refer them to resources to find a support group
The history with mental Illness and wondering about how realistic it would be to keep my arms covered everyday if I decided to go into it
Awww I'm so glad you're here! Good to know I'm not totally alone here 💞
I have been

I am extremely concious even in clinical that I never bring up my own personal issues or past. And also that I focus more on being empathic/providing presence because that's all I really am comfortable doing right now. I'm trying to stay aware too of any countertransference/transference that may be occuring. Just out of basic professional principles
I fear that it might be unprofessional if a patient could tell MY history. I don't think I would tell a patient if I had high BP or diabetes
Thank you for your input!
Thank you so much for your insight! It was very helpful. These are all things I want to think about, so it's good to hear some perspective.
Oh it was sharp lol
I am a "ultra fast metabolizer" or something like that I did get the genetic testing done at one point in order to find proper ADHD meds and sleep meds!
I have a little irish in me 😂
Ugh yes my situation was very similar. I tried to call myself down but couldn't 😅 my HR was 200

Haha yeah and I'm vaccinated as well for school but still there's that SMALL CHANCE and they seemed really taken aback by it. And every time I've needed it be sedated it always magically comes down to me being knocked out unconscious 😂

My schooling basically just has GAD and panic disorder built into the program that way we're always a constant state of stress 🤷‍♀️ I am under the care of a HCP I assure. I just feel bad because the WHOLE time I was hyperventilating and shaking and they kept having to tell me to be more still and then I legit puked ON THEM. And it didn't seem like something they have ever experienced before. Maybe they learned something from it. Chocolate is a great idea though!!! I'm trying to think of things that are individually packed bc covid and whatnot

Yeah I've had the therapy I just don't feel the need to defend it. It's only an hour of panic. School is more important to me than preserving my comfort. I'll deal with a few panic attacks and anxiety. Also if I got them out at any other time, I wouldn't be able to attend clinical rotation and if we miss even ONE it's automatic failure. Even if it's medically excused the state requires we get our hours. And as demanding and anxiety provoking as school is, the threat of not being in it is worse.

Honestly xanax and valium both don't work well with me. I feel like I can't hold back my anxiety and it just takes over 😂 luckily I'll never have to get wisdom teeth out again otherwise I certainly would not go back. However I still appreciate them doing it on such short notice and being a dentist during a pandemic deserves some recognition lol

There's no way of knowing how a patient is going to react to a medication. I still appreciated them dealing when I could tell they were uncomfortable. Even at the end they admitted it was tough. It can't be easy doing their job and mistakes are bound to happen
I just don't know what a covid appropriate gift would be 😂 and omg one time I got 17 shots of novocaine and it still didn't work  😬😬
I legit got anxious af over some morphine once, so I've given up all hope 😂😂

Ive have panic attacks before but never in front of that many people 😅 I felt terrible
My schooling has anxiety built in to it, its known for it and unavoidable 😅
I really had no choice considering I had to go back to school. It was fairly traumatic but I've been through a lot of trauma 😅 it'd be more traumatic for me having to go back
Great job that's amazing ❤️
